topic: Dynamic Linking and Loading of ELF Programs
explanation: Dynamic linking is a process where a program's required libraries are loaded into memory only when the program is executed, rather than being linked statically at compile time.  This reduces the program's size and allows multiple programs to share the same library code in memory, saving space and resources.  The ELF (Executable and Linkable Format) is a common standard for object files and executables on Unix-like systems.  Dynamic linking of ELF programs involves the loader resolving symbol references to shared libraries at runtime and loading those libraries into memory on demand.
